extracted.intended_audience: course coordinators, meeting leaders, and new mathematics instructors in college/university departments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, preparing, running, and following up a pre-semester orientation session (and related meetings) for new and continuing instructors in undergraduate mathematics programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the introduction, description, and goals before planning
rubrics_metrics.description: You should first read the introduction, the description, and the goals for the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If some goals important to your training program are not listed, add them. Adjust other parts of the meeting so it addresses these additional goals. Consult suggested readings to solidify perspective on the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the outline for running the meeting before finalizing format
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the outline for running the meeting to confirm that the suggested format is likely to succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the suggested format won't work, use its content to devise your own plan for running the meeting and adjust preparations, agenda, and meeting materials accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify preparations and agenda to chosen format
rubrics_metrics.description: After deciding on an appropriate format, read and modify the sections describing the preparations and the agenda as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume you have developed a plan and formulated an agenda to be circulated to participants; tailor materials and timing to your format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use meeting materials and handouts appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Each chapter provides a checklist of meeting materials, handouts, and supporting documents to distribute before, during, or after the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If meeting descriptions are followed closely, supporting documents will be most useful if given in advance or during the meeting. Choose distribution timing to best serve meeting goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt or replace materials incompatible with institutional customs
rubrics_metrics.description: If included meeting materials conflict with your institution’s guidelines or customs, produce a similar document reflecting institutional practices or opt to distribute nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you distribute nothing, modify the agenda and outline for running the meeting to account for the lack of handouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow a flexible time-line for meeting preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a suggested flexible time-line for preparations but adapt it to your situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended timing: 10–14 days before—meet with executives to develop objectives and decide if meeting is necessary; 7–10 days—plan agenda and decide attendees; one week—reserve room, announce meeting, circulate agenda; 5–7 days—read and modify meeting description; 1–5 days—prepare materials; day of—reread goals and conduct meeting; 1–3 days after—follow up on effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce meetings with adequate advance notice (about one week minimum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants appreciate as much advance warning as possible, but one week is considered the minimum amount of notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too-far-in-advance announcements may be forgotten and some participants may deliberately schedule conflicts; try alternative venues to relay vital information to absentees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start meetings with introductions and reiteration of goals
rubrics_metrics.description: At the introduction, thank participants and reiterate the goals or objectives for the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simply reciting goals has little impact—write goals on a chalkboard or display them on a transparency to be more effective. Hand out institutional guidelines that may apply to the topic during the introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: End meetings with summary, Q&A, and distribution of follow-up materials
rubrics_metrics.description: End by summarizing important points, providing time for participants’ questions, handing out suggestions for additional readings, or distributing questionnaires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose which activities to include depending on meeting type and goals. If time is short, ask participants to bring questions individually after the meeting or distribute summaries as they leave. Always thank participants before they leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use questionnaires early, then discontinue when not yielding new information
rubrics_metrics.description: A questionnaire is provided; in practice it will probably only be necessary for the first few meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After two or three meetings you should develop an accurate picture of participants' likes and dislikes; when questionnaires no longer develop new useful information, stop using them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques for expediting meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: If meetings need to be abbreviated, use specific techniques to expedite them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques include: distribute handouts to be read prior to the meeting; assign suggested activities as prework and hold only discussion during the meeting; distill discussions into a handout; ask experienced instructors to prepare one-page handouts describing experiences; use role-play demonstrations or written vignettes in place of active role-play; distribute questionnaires for later return (but expect lower return rates); if primary function is dissemination, consider not holding a meeting and simply distribute guidelines (but beware many will not read them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide whether to hold a meeting (decision checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before deciding to have a meeting, consider specific questions about program goals and necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions include: What are the goals/objectives for the next two weeks? Is a large meeting essential to achieve these goals? Are there meetings in the book that can help achieve the goals?

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation checklist for meeting leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a meeting, ensure you have completed essential preparation steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items: have you done the reading for the meeting? What meeting format will work? What should be on the agenda? Who needs to attend? Do you have a suitable time/day and room? Have you given participants enough warning (one week at least)? What about people who cannot attend? Are the meeting materials suitable or need modification? Have you made enough copies? Have you done everything in the 'Preparation for the Meeting' section? Have you reread the meeting description? Do you have everything needed for the meeting?

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up checklist after a meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: After a meeting, evaluate its effectiveness and handle outstanding issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions to ask: What made the meeting effective? What could make the next meeting more effective? Have you followed up on unanswered questions? Have the people who missed the meeting been dealt with appropriately?

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing new meetings (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: If training program goals are not addressed by provided meetings, use Chapter 16 to develop new meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: identify additional goals, gather resource materials (departmental documents, MAA notes, journal articles, literature on classroom practices), then use Chapter 16 methods to fashion these resources into a training meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use class visits as part of professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Class visits can give feedback to individual instructors, personalize professional development, and inform course coordinators about program effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course coordinators should read the purposes and goals for class visits, modify goals to department needs, read the four sections detailing visit types and weigh advantages/disadvantages, develop a schedule, and consult 'Ideas for Using Visits Throughout the Semester' to combine visits. Assemble teams of visitors if many observations planned; prepare for potential implementation problems (see Section 17.6); maintain confidentiality and report back to course coordinator to customize future training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit facilitator load during class visits
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unreasonable for one facilitator to attend and give feedback for more than five classes per week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an extensive program of visits is planned, assemble a team of visitors to assist with observations and feedback; divide instructors among facilitators and have each re-read the relevant visit-type section prior to visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare visitor team via workshop or practice observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare facilitators by re-reading sections and optionally running a workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A thorough approach is to develop a workshop for facilitators including practice observing and giving feedback or observing and discussing videotapes of actual classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: articulate course goals clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide new instructors with a clear articulation of the goals of the course they are expected to teach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate goals in terms of national reform and institutional purposes; refer instructors to an overhead and course handbook where goals are summarized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: provide lesson design examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide new instructors with examples of how other teachers have designed lessons to try to achieve course goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand out sample lesson plans, discuss their features, and show how they tie to course goals and student-centered instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: introduce required technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce new instructors to the technology (calculators, computer algebra systems) they will be expected to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a brief activity exploring basic skills; demonstrate graphing and problem-solving uses; alert instructors to later in-semester meetings focusing on meaningful technology use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: introduce grading systems and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce new instructors to the grading systems and conventions typically used in the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute a sample grading scheme that weights assessment components; discuss gateway exams, historical grade averages, institutional meanings of grades, student interpretations, and stress having a well-defined grading scheme to hand out on the first day that should not be modified later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: indicate first-day issues and required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate to new instructors the issues and opportunities of the first day and what materials they should create for that meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a sample first-day handout/syllabus and a student data sheet to gather student information for group formation and name-learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: familiarize instructors with administrative duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarize instructors with the administrative duties required at the beginning of the semester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute departmental and university expectations, calendar, and procedural handouts either verbally or in written form (preferably written where no response is required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: introduce student-centered instruction methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an introduction to the methods of student-centered instruction likely to be used on the first day or during the first week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast traditional transmission model with constructivist/active student models; emphasize minimizing lecturing and incorporating learning activities, cooperative learning, and pre-class textbook reading expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: provide guidance on tests, quizzes, and grading fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instructors with guidelines regarding tests and quizzes usually given and how these items are graded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the role of quizzes, design and grading methods, the psychology of marking papers, and practice grading activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: provide practice organizing and presenting explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Give instructors an opportunity to practice organizing an explanation and presenting it to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include practice teaching exercises (Block C) and provide feedback; arrange visits to master teachers' classrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: provide feedback on presentation skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an opportunity for instructors to receive feedback on their presentation skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use practice teaching sessions, peer feedback, and facilitator comments; schedule classroom visits early in semester for novice instructors to observe master teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: provide opportunity to critically observe other teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instructors with an opportunity to critically observe other teachers and consider how to apply observations in their own classrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize visits to master teachers and follow-up discussions; encourage trainees to reflect and adapt observed practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: schedule novice visits to master teachers early
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize a program of visits by novice instructors to master teachers’ classrooms early in the semester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange a system of first-week visits and ensure scheduling/logistics are handled by training staff; follow up with confidentiality and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session goal: provide preliminary indicators for in-semester focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training staff with an indicator of areas of instructor development on which in-semester training should focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use initial observations, questionnaires, practice teaching feedback, and early classroom visits to identify developmental priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize orientation into three blocks by instructor experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide orientation into Block A (all instructors), Block B (novice and journeyman), and Block C (primarily novice) to address differing training needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Block A covers departmental resources, conventions, grading, technology basics; Block B introduces student-centered practices and grading issues; Block C provides practice teaching, visits, and feedback. Adapt format to trainee mix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a course handbook containing essential course and departmental information
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a course handbook that codifies useful information for new instructors and is distributed during Block A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested items to include: departmental philosophies and course goals; responsibilities of training staff and instructors; overview of weekly meetings; description of how instructors’ teaching will be evaluated and what information will be used for; description of the textbook and course technology and how these fit course goals; a sample first-day handout; a sample student data sheet; a semester day-to-day schedule; recommended homework problems; university and departmental expectations; departmental resources (computers, copiers, office supplies, secretarial support); sample exams from prior semesters; overview of the student population; departmental curriculum context; necessary grade information (policy, historical averages, sample grading scheme); university calendar with important dates; description of student support services available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use overheads and guided discussion to situate course goals and teaching philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use overheads to articulate course goals, summarize the training program, and discuss how new instructors' performances will be evaluated and used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why particular goals are important, situate them within national trends, and discuss constructivist ideas and vocabulary used throughout the training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sample lesson plans and highlight their important features
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand out at least one week’s worth of sample lesson plans and lead discussion tying them to course goals and student-centered learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important features to emphasize include learning activities in class, limits on lecturing, cooperative learning, use of calculators/technology to investigate mathematics, assessment aligned with course goals, and planning lessons assuming students have read the textbook prior to class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a brief, hands-on technology introduction during orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead a short presentation on calculator/computer basics and simple in-class activities to familiarize instructors with platform basics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give instructors short exercises (e.g., optimization problems solved via graphing calculators) and allow Q&A; emphasize that later in-semester training will focus on meaningful use beyond basics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribute and explain grading schemes and evaluation techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Make instructors aware of common evaluation techniques used in the department and pass out a sample grading scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss weighting of assessment components (exams, quizzes, homework, team projects, writing, portfolios, presentations, lab assignments), gateway exams, historical grade averages, institutional meanings of grades, and the importance of providing a well-defined grading scheme on the first day that should not be modified later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sample first-day handout and student data form
rubrics_metrics.description: Pass out a sample first-day handout/syllabus and a sample student data form to be used on the first day of class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data sheets to help instructors learn student names, form cooperative groups, and detect placement problems; summarize important first-day outcomes to set groundwork for a successful semester.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-day outcomes to achieve
rubrics_metrics.description: On the first day, achieve a set of outcomes to set the semester’s tone and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes include: conveying essential course information, requirements, and expectations; beginning to learn students' names and help students learn each other's names; creating an atmosphere for active learning by providing opportunities to be active participants; forming groups if cooperative learning will be used; getting students to read the textbook before next class; assigning homework if regular; and doing some mathematics in class.
